recipes.name: Blackberry Pie
ingredients_raw: 1 (9 inch) double crust ready-to-use pie crust

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
Combine 3 ½ cups of blackberries with 1/2 cup sugar and flour in a large bowl. Spoon mixture into the unbaked pie crust. Spread remaining 1/2 cup of blackberries on top of sweetened berries.
Cover with the top crust. Seal and crimp the edges, and cut vents in the top crust for steam to escape.
Brush the top crust with milk and sprinkle with remaining 1/4 cup sugar.

Bake pie in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce the temperature of the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) and bake until filling is bubbly and crust is golden brown, an additional 20 to 25 minutes. Cool on wire rack.

raw_recipe.headline: Blackberry Pie
raw_recipe.description: This tasty blackberry pie recipe is so simple to make with store-bought pie crust. Use fresh or frozen blackberries and serve with vanilla ice cream.

video.description: In this video, Nicole shows you how to make a homemade blackberry pie with a sweet crust. This dessert recipe starts with tossing the blackberries in sugar and flour before placing them in the crust to give them a creamy sauce for the inside of the pie. After rolling the second crust over the top, brush with milk and sprinkle sugar over it before baking in the oven. With a sugary crust and the juicy blackberries, this classic pie is a perfect summer dessert!

review.reviewBody: I am somewhat of a fussy pie baker and I loved this recipe! The only things I did differently were that I used 5 pints of large berries, I also brushed the bottom crust with a little beaten egg, squeezed a little lemon juice over the berries and dotted with butter before putting the top crust on. I brushed the top crust with some of the beaten egg and sprinkled sugar over it. It was delicious and I agree, serve this with a little vanilla ice-cream. I've made this pie about 5 times this summer and received rave reviews each time. One more tip ~ make sure that you combine the berries with the sugar and flour well until you no longer see any "white" coating on the berries.

Very good. I added more berries, and it still fit well into the pie dish. Next time I would squeeze a tablespoon or so of lemon juice on top for a needed brightness. I used 1/4 cup tapioca in lieu of the flour. I did brush some beaten egg onto the bottom crust to keep it from becoming soggy.

This is delicious! I used a bag of frozen blackberries and increased the bake time to 30 minutes. I would recommend only brushing the pie with one tablespoon of milk before sprinkling the sugar, as two made the top a little watery-still delicious though!

I've made this as written as well as with recommendations from reviews. The additions make this a stellar dessert. I can't imagine why anyone would want 1/4 cup sugar on top of their pie and saturate it with 2 whole tablespoons of milk. One tablespoon milk is enough, and and 1-2 tsps of sugar is really all you need on top. The pie was runny with flour, so I replaced the flour with 1/4 cup of instant, granulated tapioca. Once it cooled completely, the pie didn't run at all. Squeeze half a lemon over the berries and sprinkle 2 tablespoons of chopped butter over them as well before topping off the pie with the second crust. Brushing the bottom with egg saves the pie from getting soggy on the bottom. Absolutely amazing on a hot summer day with French Vanilla ice cream!

After making this pie for the first time last week, my friends have been calling me and asking if I've made another (which I did :)). I have a deep pie dish, so I added 2 cups of blueberries for a "black-n-blueberry pie." It doesn't seem too 'oozie', and it's really delicious!

Yum! This pie is divine. A perfect way to use up all those blackberries in the garden. I usually use blackberries that aren't sweet enough to eat plain, and increase the amount of sugar in the pie. I also find the juice of half a lemon really wakes it up, and some egg wash brushed on the bottom crust keeps it from turning soggy. Dots of butter beneath the top layer of crust don't hurt either! While frozen berries work fine, I really prefer the taste of fresh ones. This basic recipe holds up well to personal tweaks. Sometimes I like to add orange or lime zest and a squeeze of juice to the filling. Occasionally I make this pie with mixed berries (strawberries, raspberries, blueberries...) and it always turns out splendidly.

I loved this dish! Having never made this dish before and being 14 it was fairly easier than I thought it would be. I bought a 9" pie crust bowl from Walmart for the bottom and pillsbury rolled pie crust from Safeway to cover the top. Some tips and things that weren't very clear to me are: if you think the mixture is really watery don't be afraid to add more blackberries! One of mine (I made 2) was more watery than I liked. Also if you tast it it will tast floured down but once it cooks it will be fine (but adding a little more sugar never hurt nobody). Next, adding a layer of blackberries that weren't mixed with the flour/sugar combo on the top of the filling is SUPER IMPORTANT!!! You need to put a whole layer of blackberries covering all of the combo berries or else the juices will soak the covering dough and will not cook right! So save more than just a half cup for the top (If that made sense). Also like a other person suggested, one tablespoon of milk and sugar for the top was more than enough for my pies. I also whisked up a egg to cost the bottom because there were some cracks and it helped keep the bottom crust from getting soaked. I definitely will make this again maybe even experimenting with some lemon! And i can't imagin me trying it without ice cream because it was the best! Hope this helped you!!!

I added 1/4 cup more sugar because my berries were froze and lost some sweetness from the time of picking them fresh. I brushed beaten egg to the bottom crust prior to filling with berries and the top crust with beaten egg instead of milk. I added 3/4 teaspoon lemon juice to the flour, sugar, berry mixture after it was COMPLETELY mixed and slightly soupy appearing. I added the last 1/4 teaspoon lemon juice to just the berries on top of the sweetened mixture. I used a deep dish pie pan (glass) and probably could have used 1 cup of berries on top of the mixture. I also used 2 tablespoons of butter cut into small pieces on top of the berry mixture prior to the top crust. I baked 30 minutes and let it sit in the stove for an extra 10-15 minutes with no heat before removing. Let it set at least two hours on wire rack before cutting. Perfection!

This was the first pie recipe I've ever made, so I was a bit apprehensive. However, it came out pretty good for the first try! I used the crust recipe on the Crisco can, and made this filling with fresh blackberries. After reading reviews about using tapioca flour, I figured I should use it. However, I had xantham gum on hand already so I used just under a 1/2 cup of flour, and then maybe a teaspoon of xantham gum. It was a clean slice - not runny at all! I also brushed the bottom crust with egg wash before filling. 

Not sure if I was supposed to, but when mixing the blackberries with the flour/sugar/xantham gum, I mashed them a bit to make it into a gooey filling. The directions don't specify to do that, but I think you're supposed to. 

Also I subbed coconut sugar for white sugar - next time I will increase the amount just a bit.

Loved the simplicity and versatility of this recipe! I added a dash of lemon juice the second time round just to add a little more brightness to it, and the third time round I swapped the top crust for a simple crumble. Definitely a delicious way to use up all the extra blackberries I had growing this year!

First time I ever made a pie. I made it for my boyfriend's birthday. It turned out perfect. I did add beaten egg to the bottom of the crust. I also put a little flour on the bottom crust to keep from sticking to the glass pan. I dotted butter on the blackberries. Could have used more blackberries. I would recommend 5 cups. Also a little lemon juice on top(another viewer suggested). The pie was delicious just a little to tart for my taste which is why I recommend the lemon juice. Also I did change the top crust. I used about 1 1/2 tsp melted butter brushed on and sprinkled the sugar on top as directed. It was a hit and he is already asking for another pie!!!!
Flour was everywhere. None of it combined in the pie. Literally baked it for 1 hour and 30 min, just in an attempt to get any of the ingredients to combine.
Great, easy recipe perfect
This recipe is awesome! Definitely a keeper
Cut the sugar by 1/2 and maybe 1 tbls of sugar sprinkled on the crust. Otherwise, this recipe is overly sweet.
Definitely a keeper. Could use less sugar on top and in the filling, but it was a hit as is!

Picked the berries this morning and used tonight recipe tonight. I always add a punch of Saigon cinnamon when cooking with blackberries. It just adds that extra kiss of yum. This is a keeper!! Thank you!
Would have liked it a little juicer. But we are eating it! Our berries were big from our garden!
I honestly enjoyed the flavor.
This recipe was a big hit for Christmas
